label: MORNING BRIEF

stories.title: Kampala traders end their strike
stories.story: Traders ended their three-day shutdown after government promised to review taxes on imported clothes. Cabinet gives its answer on 24 Nov.
stories.you: Shops are reopening. Restart shop viewings — and watch Cabinet’s reply.

stories.title: Dollar climbs to Shs4,225
stories.story: The shilling weakened on 18 Nov, closing at 4,225 a dollar after opening at 4,180. Traders blame strong demand for dollars.
stories.you: Dollar earners get more shillings. Show diaspora buyers the dollar price too.

stories.title: Bududa: move out by December
stories.story: Families in Bududa’s high-risk areas have two months to leave. Government offers Shs18m: two acres worth Shs8m and Shs10m to build a house.
stories.you: Families will be buying land. Offer safe, titled plots in the east.

stories.title: Minerals under land belong to the State
stories.story: Minister Phiona Nyamutoro warned Kigezi landowners not to block mining. If talks fail, the law allows compulsory acquisition, valued by the Chief Government Valuer.
stories.you: Selling land in a mineral area? Check for mining licences before your client pays.

stories.title: Masaka industrial park is back on
stories.story: Government has revived the park at Mazigo, Bukakata, 11 years after its 2015 launch. Chinese investors have visited the site, which is meant for coffee processing.
stories.you: Buyers may ask. Sell the land, not the promise — this park stalled for years.
